svg.title: A posterior tail and a sampling tail are different pictures
svg.desc: Left: the Beta(28, 16) posterior with the region above 0.5 shaded and labelled 0.9670. Right: the binomial distribution of germination counts when the rate is exactly one half, with the counts of twenty-six or more shaded and labelled 0.0403.
svg.text: Read it as: given these forty seeds and the Beta(2, 2)
prior, the probability that the germination rate is above
one half is 0.9670. The unknown rate is what varies here;
the data are fixed at what happened.
germinations in a tray of forty, if pi is 0.5
Read it as: if the rate were exactly one half, the
probability of seeing twenty-six or more germinations is
0.0403. The rate is held fixed at one half here; the data
0.9670 and 1 minus 0.0403, which is 0.9597, are close together. They address different questions, and the
closeness comes from a weak prior rather than from any equivalence.
